builder_plan.scenario: A product assistant retrieves plausible documents but gives unsupported answers.
builder_plan.change: Change one retrieval or ranking step while keeping the document snapshot fixed.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current retrieval pipeline with identical questions and answer model.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Supported answers, retrieval misses, correct abstentions, index cost, and response latency.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: A Hybrid RAG Framework for Deceptive Review Detection: Integrating RoBERTa-LoRA, FAISS-Based Retrieval, and LLM Reasoning
summary: Replaces a single fine-tuned classifier or a zero-shot LLM detector with a three-stage pipeline: RoBERTa-LoRA classification, FAISS retrieval of similar labeled reviews, and LLM reasoning over retrieved evidence for explainable verdicts. Costs include maintaining a FAISS index of labeled domain data, per-query LLM API latency and expense on top of local inference, and added orchestration complexity across three components. Can fail when the retrieval corpus does not cover the target domain (the 0.90 cross-domain F1 trails the 0.97 in-domain model), when LLM API costs scale with review volume, or when the LLM reasoning layer introduces errors not caught by the classifier.
rationale: The pipeline is buildable on a single 24 GB GPU plus an LLM API, but the hybrid's advantage over the plain fine-tuned classifier is reported only for deceptive review detection and needs validation on the reader's own data distribution and cost constraints.
technique: Hybrid RAG with LoRA classifier and LLM reasoning

claims.statement: Replaces a single fine-tuned classifier or a zero-shot LLM detector with a three-stage pipeline: RoBERTa-LoRA classification, FAISS retrieval of similar labeled reviews, and LLM reasoning over retrieved evidence for explainable verdicts. Costs include maintaining a FAISS index of labeled domain data, per-query LLM API latency and expense on top of local inference, and added orchestration complexity across three components. Can fail when the retrieval corpus does not cover the target domain (the 0.90 cross-domain F1 trails the 0.97 in-domain model), when LLM API costs scale with review volume, or when the LLM reasoning layer introduces errors not caught by the classifier.
Cross-domain F1 of 0.90 after five LoRA fine-tuning epochs, versus 0.82 for the OpenAI Detector baseline; in-domain specialized SOTA (fakeRoBERTa) still reaches 0.97.
